summary: Built an IKEv2/IPsec (libreswan) site-to-site tunnel between node1 and node2 over a dedicated transit segment (172.16.0.0/30 on eth1), routing node3's private LAN (192.168.10.0/24, behind node1 on eth2) and node4's private LAN (192.168.20.0/24, behind node2 on eth2) across it. node3 and node4 now reach each other by their private addresses, and all cross-network traffic on the transit wire is ESP-encrypted (verified by packet capture showing only ESP frames, no plaintext). Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all four nodes with boot-id proof and full post-restart recovery of network config, the IPsec tunnel, and end-to-end connectivity.
actions_performed: Mapped physical topology via ARP/bridge-id fingerprinting: node1 eth1 and node2 eth1 share a common transit L2 segment; node1 eth2 faces node3's enp8s0 (lan-a); node2 eth2 faces node4's enp8s0 (lan-b)
Configured UCI network interfaces on node1/node2: 'transit' (172.16.0.1/30, 172.16.0.2/30) and 'lana'/'lanb' (192.168.10.1/24, 192.168.20.1/24) on eth1/eth2
Assigned static private IPs on node3 (192.168.10.10) and node4 (192.168.20.10) via NetworkManager on enp8s0, with explicit static routes to the remote private subnet via the local router

Reworked OpenWrt firewall: repurposed the pre-staged 'wan' zone for the transit network (input ACCEPT for IKE/ESP, masquerade disabled to preserve private source addresses end-to-end), added lana/lanb zones with bidirectional forwarding to/from the transit zone
Added static routes on node1/node2 for the remote private subnet via the transit peer address

Installed libreswan via apk on node1/node2; generated a PSK from node1's /dev/urandom and transferred it to node2 over the private transit link via a temporary uhttpd-served file (SSH between nodes hit a dropbear client transport quirk), then deleted the temp file

Configured the tunnel via the OpenWrt-native /etc/config/libreswan UCI tunnel section (auto=start, IKEv2, PSK) so the init script auto-establishes the tunnel on service start/boot instead of a manual raw ipsec.d/*.conf that the init script ignores
Verified plaintext routing worked before enabling encryption (baseline), then verified the tunnel encrypts (ESP-only on the wire) and node3<->node4 ping succeeds by private address in both directions
Captured healthy baseline (boot IDs, tunnel/erouted state, IKE/IPsec SA counts, interface/route config, service-enabled flags) on all 4 nodes

Restarted node1, node2, node3, node4 one at a time (native reboot/systemctl reboot), confirmed acknowledgement before disconnect, polled until exec access returned, proved changed boot IDs on each, and verified full recovery of network config, IPsec SA/erouted state, and end-to-end private connectivity after each restart before moving to the next node

evidence.summary: Bridge-id and ARP/DHCP-broadcast capture on node1/node2 eth1 vs eth2 confirmed eth1-eth1 is the shared transit segment and eth2 faces node3/node4 respectively

evidence.requirement: Private networks route to each other by private address
evidence.summary: Baseline: node3->node4 by private IP failed pre-tunnel (net unreachable / silent drop); after full config, node3 pings 192.168.20.10 and node4 pings 192.168.10.10 successfully with 0% loss

evidence.requirement: Traffic between private networks is encrypted in transit
evidence.summary: ip xfrm policy/state show active AES-CBC-256/HMAC-SHA2-256 ESP SAs; tcpdump on node1 eth1 (transit wire) during a node3->node4 ping shows only ESP(spi=...) frames, no plaintext ICMP on the wire

evidence.requirement: IPsec tunnel establishes automatically (persists across restarts), not just manually
evidence.summary: Tunnel converted from manual ipsec.d/*.conf (not auto-loaded by OpenWrt's init script) to native /etc/config/libreswan UCI tunnel with auto=start; ipsec restart alone re-establishes the erouted tunnel with authenticated IKE/IPsec SAs on both nodes without manual intervention

evidence.requirement: Baseline healthy state captured before any restart (node1)
evidence.summary: Pre-restart boot_id fe443453... and healthy erouted tunnel/interface/route/service-enabled state captured for node1

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: reboot command acknowledged (connection closed), exec unreachable during reboot, boot_id changed to 3414995f... on recovery, and network/route/IPsec erouted state plus node3->node4 ping all recovered post-reboot

evidence.requirement: Baseline healthy state captured before any restart (node2)
evidence.summary: Pre-restart boot_id cac19401... and healthy erouted tunnel/interface/route/service-enabled state captured for node2

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: reboot acknowledged, connection timed out during reboot, boot_id changed to ba990507... on recovery, and network/route/IPsec erouted state plus node4->node3 ping recovered post-reboot

evidence.requirement: Baseline healthy state captured before any restart (node3)
evidence.summary: Pre-restart boot_id e625b9a5... and healthy private-IP/route/autoconnect config captured for node3

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot acknowledged (stream closed), unreachable during reboot, boot_id changed to e1ac730b... on recovery, private IP/route persisted, and ping to node4 succeeded post-reboot

evidence.requirement: Baseline healthy state captured before any restart (node4)
evidence.summary: Pre-restart boot_id 7223d5b7... and healthy private-IP/route/autoconnect config captured for node4

evidence.requirement: node4 restart: acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot acknowledged, unreachable during reboot, boot_id changed to 29c325bc... on recovery, private IP/route persisted, and ping to node3 succeeded post-reboot

evidence.requirement: Final post-all-restarts verification that both encryption and private-address reachability still hold
evidence.summary: After all 4 nodes were individually restarted, node3<->node4 ping by private address succeeded in both directions and node1's transit-interface capture showed only ESP frames, confirming the tunnel and encryption survived the full restart cycle
